pr_title: Remove keys from local_cache in RedisCacheStore#delete_matched
pr_body:
Fixes #38627

### Summary

Right now `RedisCacheStore#delete_matched` doesn't delete entries in local cache, which is wrong. Fix it.

issue_context.title: `RedisCacheStore#delete_matched` doesn't play well with local cache
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

  gem "rails", github: "rails/rails"
  gem 'redis'
end

require "active_support"
require "active_support/core_ext/object/blank"
require "minitest/autorun"

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_with_local_cache
    client = ActiveSupport::Cache::RedisCacheStore.new

    client.with_local_cache do
      client.write('my_key#123', 'xxx')
      client.delete_matched('my_key#*')

      # Passes
      assert client.send(:bypass_local_cache) { client.read('my_key#123') }.nil?

      # Fails
      assert client.read('my_key#123').nil?
    end
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior
Test should pass or at least rails should provide a way to handle that case without hacky `#send(:bypass_cache) { }`

### Actual behavior
Test fails, we're reading stale value from local cache.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6 & master

**Ruby version**: 2.7

review_comments:
This set will consume memory proportional to the total number of entries deleted, where the current implementation is bounded by `SCAN_BATCH_SIZE`. It's also still implicitly coupled to the local cache; there's no other reason to return this data.

How about instead clearing the local cache entirely when `delete_matched` is called? More local cache entries will be removed than strictly necessary, but it's also a much simpler approach, and I think the edge case where it would matter (a single request reads some keys, deletes some other keys with a pattern, and then reads the original keys again) is less likely to be a problem than the increased memory usage described above.

This is what the local cache does for `cleanup`, which also deletes cache entries in a implementation-specific way:

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/6a41940a965241ede9a77837169d6a329adf13d7/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache/strategy/local_cache.rb#L104-L108
